haiku-low.q1: Gateway returns 401, same as a missing key, and touches no counter.
haiku-low.q2: 100 requests per clock minute in total, since all of a customer's keys share one counter.
haiku-low.q3: 429 with Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining 0. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request is not counted, so the count does not change.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request was already counted before forwarding, the budget is not refunded, and the 500 is returned with rate-limit headers.
haiku-low.q6: Gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, forwards the request with no rate-limit headers, and does not retry. One unit may be lost.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per clock minute. Enterprise: no limit yet, so requests skip the check. The Enterprise limit is open.
haiku-low.q8: In one Redis primary, under key rl:<customerId>:<windowStart>. Keys expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q9: At each new clock minute, a new key starts at zero. Old keys expire on their own after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: The check and the increment run as one Redis Lua script, executed as a single unit with no other command in between.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After is 60 minus (now mod 60) seconds, using Redis's clock. It is the time until the next minute starts.
haiku-low.q12: No retry. The request is forwarded with no rate-limit headers, so the client gets no X-RateLimit information.

sonnet.q1: Gateway returns 401 (same as missing key); no counter is touched.
sonnet.q2: 100 requests per clock minute total; the limit is shared by all of that customer's keys.
sonnet.q3: 429 with Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The backend never sees the request (not forwarded).
sonnet.q4: No. A rejected request is not counted; the count is unchanged.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was counted before forwarding, the budget is not refunded, and the client gets the 500 with rate-limit headers.
sonnet.q6: Gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable and forwards the request anyway (fail open) with no rate-limit headers. No retry.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 per clock minute. Enterprise: no limit yet (undecided); requests skip the check.
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis primary, as a counter key rl:<customerId>:<windowStart>. Keys expire on their own after 120 seconds (EXPIRE set when count becomes 1).
sonnet.q9: At each new clock minute: a new window uses a new key, so the count starts at zero with no reset step. The old key expires on its own.
sonnet.q10: The check and increment run as one Redis Lua script, executed as a single unit with nothing in between, so only one instance can take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: 60 - (now mod 60) seconds, using Redis's clock: time until the next minute starts (1 to 59 seconds).
sonnet.q12: No retry. The client gets the backend response with no rate-limit headers; a metric is emitted. (An increment may have happened if the script ran before the deadline.)
